newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia says to step up finance sector reforms.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia says to step up finance sector reforms.

text.p: Yugoslavia's government said on Friday it will step up activity to reform its ailing financial sector and transform the local financial market before privatisation in Serbia begins.

"It is necessary to urgently resolve major problems in the financial sector. Without reforms there will be no development of the sector," the government team of experts, headed by Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Danko Djunic, said in a press release faxed to Reuters.
Reforms include a bank rehabilitation programme and further development of the financial market.

Market development measures will be finalised by October 31, when privatisation in Serbia begins, while the framework for the bank overhaul programme will be established by the end of 1997, the statement said.

Members of the expert team are the central bank governor, Yugoslav finance minister and IMF minister, Montenegrin finance minister, Serbian privatisation minister, Belgrade bourse head, Yugoslav Banking Association general secretary, head of the Bank Rehabilitation Agency and five top bankers. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 311 4254
